newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - Treasuries to ride data, outstrip Bunds.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - Treasuries to ride data, outstrip Bunds.

text.p: U.S. bonds are looking good despite a minefield of economic data this week, and will outperform rate-nervous Bunds, economists said on Monday.
"We could see the 10-year spread coming in over the next week to the 60 basis point level," said Philip Tyson, international economist at HSBC Markets in London.
The T-note/Bund spread was at 70 basis points at 1007 GMT.
The strength of the dollar, prospect of market-friendly data and the likelihood of a U.S. budget deal on Monday were helping Treasuries, analysts said.
Meanwhile, the weak mark and talk of a switch to a variable-rate repo tender were undermining Bunds, they added.

"If the U.S. market does rally, that should support the Bund market," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London. "But the fundamentals are more favourable in the U.S. at the moment."
Stamenkovic saw the 10-year T-note/Bund spread narrowing to 40 basis points by the end of the third quarter.
The dollar rose to near 7-1/2 year highs against the mark earlier on Monday ahead of a stream of data releases this week, and was trading at 1.8459/64 marks at 1023 GMT.
Markets were looking to the Employment Cost Index (ECI) for the second quarter on Tuesday, GDP data on Thursday and July payrolls on Friday.
"It is quite difficult to see anything other than the same growth-with-low-inflation story in the U.S.," said Adrian Owens, European economist at Julius Baer Investments in London.
The ECI will rise by 0.8 percent, the advance measure of real GDP for the second quarter will gain 1.9 percent and non-farm payrolls will increase by 193,000, according to a Reuters survey.
"They should all continue to point to a bit of a slowdown," said Tyson. "But there is a bit of a risk in the ECI with benefit costs."
The U.S. Treasury was also due to announce its quarterly refunding needs on Monday.

In addition, U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Sunday a wide-ranging budget and tax agreement with the Republican Congress could be completed as early as Monday if "remaining problems were resolved".
"That should herald an improving fiscal position which will be a contributory factor in the positive tone for Treasuries," said Stamenkovic.
Meanwhile, talk that the Bundesbank may need to act to strengthen the mark was holding Bunds back, analysts said.
"There is only one subject in Europe and in Germany at the moment, and that is the possible move to a variable rate repo, and an earlier than expected hike in German rates," said Owens.

The Bundesbank last week set its securities repurchase rate at a fixed three percent for the next two weeks instead of the usual four, fuelling speculation the subsequent rate will be set using a variable-rate tender.
Increasing belief that European economic and monetary union (EMU) will be launched by a broad group of countries, making for a softer euro, is weighing on the mark, analysts said.
But they added fears of a German rate rise were overdone.
"On domestic grounds there is no justification for a rate hike but the markets are more nervous, while in the U.S. a rate rise is off the agenda," said Stamenkovic.
The shorter end of the Bund market was likely to fare more badly against Treasuries, Owens said.
"The longer end will remain more underpinned, as investors are not really that worried about the inflation outlook."
